options.option_text: Indifferent (means lacking concern — not a synonym)
Philanthropic (correct: benevolent = well-meaning and kindly; philanthropic = caring for others ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. BENEVOLENT (adjective): well-meaning, charitable, kind toward others. Synonyms: philanthropic, munificent, magnanimous, altruistic. Root: bene (good) + volen (wishing). Antonym: malevolent (bene→male).

options.option_text: Transient (correct: ephemeral = lasting a very short time; transient = passing, not lasting ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. EPHEMERAL (adjective): lasting for a very short time; fleeting. Synonyms: transient, fleeting, momentary, transitory, evanescent. Antonym: eternal, permanent. Root: Greek ephemeros = 'lasting only a day' (epi + hemera/day).

options.option_text: Bitterness (correct: acrimony = bitterness or ill feeling; bitterness is the direct synonym ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. ACRIMONY (noun): bitterness, especially in speech or manner; sharp hostility. Synonyms: bitterness, rancour, asperity, acerbity, animosity. Root: Latin acer = sharp/bitter. Common context: 'The debate ended in acrimony.' Antonym: goodwill, amity.

options.option_text: Blameworthy (antonym: blame is opposite of laud)
Loud (sounds like 'laud' but means 'high in volume' — wrong)
Commendable (correct: laudable = deserving praise; commendable = worthy of commendation ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. LAUDABLE (adjective): deserving praise and commendation. Root: Latin laudare = to praise. Synonyms: commendable, praiseworthy, admirable, meritorious. Trap: 'loud' sounds similar but is unrelated. Antonym: blameworthy, reprehensible.

options.option_text: Hinder (correct: impede = delay or prevent by obstructing; hinder = make difficult ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. IMPEDE (verb): delay or block the progress of; obstruct. Synonyms: hinder, obstruct, hamper, retard, thwart. Root: Latin impedire = to put shackles on feet (in + pes/foot). Antonym: expedite, facilitate. Exam context: 'Bureaucracy impedes progress.'

options.option_text: Impudent (correct: insolent = rude and disrespectful; impudent = bold disrespect ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. INSOLENT (adjective): showing a rude and arrogant lack of respect. Synonyms: impudent, impertinent, insubordinate, brazen, audacious. Root: Latin insolens = unaccustomed, haughty. Antonym: respectful, deferential.

options.option_text: Garrulous (correct: loquacious = excessively talkative; garrulous = pointlessly talkative ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. LOQUACIOUS (adjective): tending to talk a great deal; talkative. Root: Latin loqui = to speak (also: elocution, eloquent, colloquial). Synonyms: garrulous, voluble, verbose, talkative. Antonym: taciturn, reticent, laconic, reserved.

options.option_text: Thrifty (correct: frugal = sparing with money/food; thrifty = avoiding waste ✓)
Lavish (antonym: lavish = very generous, sumptuously rich)

questions.explanation: B is correct. FRUGAL (adjective): sparing or economical, particularly regarding food or money; avoiding waste. Synonyms: thrifty, economical, parsimonious (extreme), penny-wise. Antonym: extravagant, lavish, profligate. Note: frugal has positive connotation (wise saving); miserly/stingy has negative (excessive).

options.option_text: Wicked (correct: nefarious = wicked; infamous for being wicked ✓)

questions.explanation: C is correct. NEFARIOUS (adjective): wicked or criminal; flagrantly villainous. Root: Latin nefas = crime/sin (ne = not + fas = divine law). Synonyms: wicked, villainous, heinous, iniquitous, depraved. Exam context: 'nefarious activities', 'nefarious plot'.

options.option_text: Dexterous (correct: adroit = clever/skilful; dexterous = showing skill with hands/mind ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. ADROIT (adjective): clever or skilful in using hands or mind. Root: French adroit = to the right (historically 'right' implied dexterity). Synonyms: dexterous, nimble, proficient, adept. Antonym: clumsy, awkward, inept. Memory hook: 'à droit' (French: to the right) → adroit/dexterous (dexter = right in Latin).

options.option_text: Yielding (antonym: yielding = ready to give way)
Stubborn (correct: obdurate = stubbornly refusing to change; stubborn = similar ✓)

questions.explanation: B is correct. OBDURATE (adjective): stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action; hardened against persuasion. Root: Latin obdurare = to harden. Synonyms: stubborn, inflexible, intransigent, implacable, recalcitrant. Antonym: yielding, amenable, pliable.

options.option_text: Worsen (antonym: ameliorate = to make something bad better)
Mitigate (partially correct: mitigate = lessen severity; ameliorate = improve, broader meaning)
Improve (correct: ameliorate = make something bad better; improve is the closest synonym ✓)

questions.explanation: D is correct. AMELIORATE (verb): make something bad better; to improve. Root: Latin melior = better. Synonyms: improve, better, enhance, alleviate, rectify. Antonym: worsen, aggravate, deteriorate, exacerbate. Commonly tested on SSC/Bank exams in sentences about reform and policy.
